walkthroughs.body_html:
Small organisms have a high SA:V and can exchange across the skin.

A 2 cm cube: SA = 6 × (2 × 2) = 24, V = 8, ratio 3:1. A 4 cm cube: SA 96, V 64, ratio 1.5:1.

Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume.

70 bpm × 70 ml = 4900 ml/min ≈ 5 litres per minute.

Tidal volume is air per normal breath (~0.5 dm³). Breathing rate is breaths per minute.

Minute ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate. 0.5 × 12 = 6 dm³/min at rest.

options: Decreases
Increases
Stays the same
Doubles each time
Heart rate × stroke volume
Heart rate ÷ stroke volume
Stroke volume ÷ heart rate
Heart rate + stroke volume

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
Active transport only happens in animals and facilitated diffusion only in plants.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes active transport from facilitated diffusion?
options: Active transport only happens in animals and facilitated diffusion only in plants.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
Active transport requires energy (ATP) and can move substances against the concentration gradient.
Both move substances down a concentration gradient, but active transport is faster.
